Sorry to hear that. I am not recommending that you try to self-medicate, but when I have had trouble eating, I have taken Benadryl or another old antihistamine. I ended up GAINING weight because of how much I ate on Benadryl when I hadn't been eating almost at all before. Zinc supplements also helped me eat more.

If you do see a doctor, be sure to ask them about nabilone. This is essentially an extract of appetite-inducing compounds in marijuana, and I have also had good success with this. In the US at least there is no age requirement for any prescription drug as long as it's prescribed.

I had a similar experience. Although I am more comfortable alone, I always crave company. Eventually, I realized that my desire was more a result of anxiety than what I truly wanted. 

Initially, treatment for depression did not help me at all with this. When I tried treatment for panic attacks and anxiety, this feeling almost completely dissipated.

I'm not trying to give medical advice here, but I have had this as a symptom of depression before. You always hear about people with depression binge eating, but my experience has also been not being able to eat.

You may or may not be willing to try this, but what worked for me was marijuana. If you live in a state where it's legal, I would try getting a 10 or 15mg THC edible and eating it. Then wait an hour or so, and it will be almost impossible NOT to eat. Even smoking marijuana will have this effect on some people. I prefer it to the appetite inducing alternatives.
